comments.author: ANadrowski
comments.body:
Hello @amihaiemil 

To be honest, the hardest part for a beginner here is understand how to run the projects together when it is needed (self-web, self-storage, self-core and self-pm). I mean.. for example: when you are implementing some new feature in "self-core", how do you run it? what are the steps? I know that it is a dumb question, but the answer is not so obvious to beginners..

comments.author: amihaiemil
comments.body:
@ANadrowski 

Well, "features" in self-core are actually new classes and methods. You cannot run self-core on its own because it's just a component. You write unit tests in order to verify that the class or method you implemented is correct.

Same for self-storage: it's just a component which you "run" by writing tests. self-storage has more sophisticated tests which run against a real database - they are called integration tests.

self-web and self-pm are spring boot apps which you can run from IntelliJ, but manual testing is not so valuable. In the case of self-web, for instance, we might write Selenium tests later on: UI Automation for end-to-end automated testing.

@criske the PR has to be merged *before* the deadline. If the deadline passes, the Task is taken away and no payments will be made to the Contributor -- payments will be made only to the PR reviewer (that is treated as a different Task).

Maybe we could allow the PO or ARCH to reassign a Contributor even if they were resigned.
